concept_panel.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
concept_panel.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant source material before asking a model to answer. Embeddings turn text into vectors so semantic search can find related chunks. RAG is useful when facts change or must be grounded in private documents. Low retrieval confidence should trigger clarification or fallback rather than invented answers.
key_takeaways: Embeddings power semantic retrieval.
Retrieved context grounds the model answer.
Low confidence needs fallback behavior.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand AI correctness, freshness, and hallucination control.
concept_panel.practical_example: Retrieve the latest refund policy before generating a customer-support answer.

questions.prompt: A support assistant invents refund rules not present in policy docs. What is the risk?
questions.explanation: LLMs can produce plausible unsupported claims. Retrieval, citations, refusals, and evals reduce that risk.

concept_panel.title: Production AI Integration
concept_panel.explanation: AI features are product systems, not just prompts. They need data handling, retrieval when facts matter, evaluation, latency/cost controls, privacy decisions, and fallback behavior. LLMs can hallucinate, so systems should ground answers in sources and measure quality repeatedly. The right architecture depends on risk and freshness requirements.
key_takeaways: RAG helps with changing factual knowledge.
Evals catch quality regressions.
Privacy and observability must be designed up front.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can design AI features as reliable software systems.
concept_panel.practical_example: A support assistant retrieves policy chunks, builds a grounded prompt, validates the answer, and logs document IDs for review.

questions.prompt: Latency and cost are too high for a summarization feature. Which trade-off might help?
questions.explanation: Quantization or smaller models can reduce cost and latency, but may reduce accuracy. Evals decide whether the trade-off is acceptable.
options: Use a smaller or quantized model and evaluate quality
questions.answer: Use a smaller or quantized model and evaluate quality

concept_panel.title: Model Quantization Trade-off
concept_panel.explanation: Quantization reduces the precision of model weights or activations so the model uses less memory and may run faster. The trade-off is that quality can drop, especially on harder tasks. Production teams should evaluate accuracy, latency, and cost together before choosing a quantized model. It is an engineering trade-off, not a universal upgrade.
key_takeaways: Quantization can reduce memory and latency.
Quality may decrease.
Evals decide whether the trade-off is acceptable.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can reason about AI system performance trade-offs.
concept_panel.practical_example: A smaller quantized summarizer may meet latency targets but needs evaluation against full-precision output.

questions.prompt: A team ships an AI feature after trying five happy-path prompts manually. What is missing?
questions.explanation: Manual prompt trials do not show regression risk. Evals provide repeatable quality checks across realistic cases.

questions.prompt: A feature sends customer medical notes to a third-party model without review. What is the primary issue?
questions.explanation: Sensitive data needs clear consent, minimization, retention policy, and vendor controls before model use.

concept_panel.title: Responsible Data Use
concept_panel.explanation: Data is both value and risk. Responsible systems define why data is collected, how long it is retained, who can access it, and how access is audited. Privacy, consent, deletion, and security requirements should be part of design rather than afterthoughts. Keeping everything forever because storage is cheap creates legal and human risk.
key_takeaways: Collect only data needed for a defined purpose.
Retention and deletion policies limit risk.
Auditability and access control make use accountable.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand ethics, privacy, and governance in data systems.
concept_panel.practical_example: Sensitive production data access should require permission, logging, and a clear business purpose.
